verdict: Wabtec grew sales 8% to $3.1B and widened margins in both rail segments, lifting GAAP earnings per share 34% — demand for freight and transit equipment stayed strong.

segments.name: Freight
segments.note: Locomotives, freight-car parts and digital rail systems — up 6.9% YoY, earning a 23.0% operating margin.

segments.name: Transit
segments.note: Passenger-rail brakes, doors and couplers — up 11.3% YoY, helped by the Dellner Couplers acquisition, at a 16.4% margin.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Selling and running the company day to day.

opex.name: Amortization
opex.note: Non-cash amortization of brands and technology bought in past deals.

otherDetail: Interest expense, net of $80M, partly offset by $12M of other income, for a net cost of $68M.
oneTimers: Adjusted EPS of $2.83 excludes $89M of non-cash amortization of acquisition intangibles (worth $0.39 a share after tax) and $4M of after-tax restructuring and portfolio-optimization costs.
footerNote: Net income of $411M is the consolidated total; $409M was attributable to Wabtec shareholders after $2M to noncontrolling interests — EPS is calculated on the $409M figure.

takeaways.title: Both segments grew
takeaways.text: Sales reached $3.12B as Freight rose 6.9% and Transit rose 11.3%, with the Frauscher and Dellner acquisitions adding to demand that was already healthy.

takeaways.title: Margins widened
takeaways.text: GAAP operating margin hit 20.0%, up 3.0 points, as gross margin improved to 37.3% — the company kept more of each sales dollar than a year ago.

takeaways.title: A record order book
takeaways.text: Backlog reached $31.4B, up 23% from a year ago — years of locomotive, parts and transit work already ordered by customers.
